title: Comparing India's data law with global standards
p1:
Your personal data is the new currency — but who controls it?

Many people assume India’s data protection rules are either as strict as Europe’s or far behind global standards. The reality is more nuanced.
p2:
India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act brings stronger rules around consent, data handling, and accountability. But unlike the European Union’s GDPR, India’s framework takes a more balanced approach between individual privacy and business needs.

A surprising difference: GDPR gives regulators broad powers to impose penalties, while India’s approach places more emphasis on government-set rules and implementation frameworks.
p3: For businesses, this means protecting customer data is no longer just an IT issue — it is a trust issue. Companies operating in India must build transparent data practices, while users need to become more aware of how their information is collected and used.
conclusion: Do you think India should move closer to Europe’s strict privacy model, or create its own approach that balances privacy with innovation?
